bib.title: Rehearse: Stepping Back from the Confidence Cliff in Self-Improving Autoresearch

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Rehearse: Stepping Back from the Confidence Cliff in Self-Improving Autoresearch", Ji Jiazhen and Ding Shouhong (Tencent), preprint arXiv:2607.27687v1 [cs.AI], 30 Jul 2026. No venue.
COVERAGE: 18 of 18 pages, all 63,344 chars read, including appendices A-I and tables. References skimmed. Figures not rendered (captions from text only). Extraction clean.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Pre-execution judgment degrades as a loop accumulates successes ("confidence cliff"). Memoryless judge: selective accuracy falls while coverage rises.
  number: 82.8% to 56.9%; coverage 76% to 85%
  setup: 366-pair benchmark (296 same-baseline worked-vs-not pairs, 70 both-worked pairs), 39 AutoSOTA tasks, mean of 3 judge models, strict consensus, bucketed by n_baseline (successes already in place), cliff = n>=3.
  quote: "a memoryless judge has 82.8% selective accuracy at cold start but only 56.9% once three or more successes have accumulated, while committing just as readily"
  where: p2 (Fig 1), Sec 4.4 p7
- Focused outcome memory restores cliff accuracy; it beats other history forms.
  number: 83.5% vs 80.9% (LLM summary), 74.1% (Reflexion-style), 70.8% (full dump), 56.9% (none). Overall 82.3% vs 77.6%.
  setup: Table 1, cliff bucket n>=3, same judge prompt, same candidate rationale. Baselines are author adaptations, not full reproductions.
  quote: "Rehearse (focused retrieval, ours) 82.3 77 83.5"
  where: Table 1, p7
- More memory is not better. Selecting only similar change+outcome lines beats the full dump drawn from the same store.
  number: 83.5% vs 70.8%; adding failure reasons to the dump gives 73.3%
  quote: "appending similarity-retrieved failure reasons to the full history reaches only 73.3% on the cliff"
  where: Sec 4.4 p7; Table 2 p9; App E
- Failure explanations hurt.
  number: 83.5% to 80.6%, and 54.8% on calls that carry a reason
  quote: "the recorded failure reason lowers cliff selective accuracy from 83.5% to 80.6%, and to 54.8% on calls that carry such a reason"
  where: Sec 4.4 p7
- Ablations (cliff, Table 2): remove candidate rationale 70.2%; remove outcome label 77.5%; worked-only precedents 78.9%; did-not-work-only 76.1%; top-1 neighbor only 80.5%.
  where: Table 2 p9, App E
- Live-loop gains. nanochat, val bpb, 30 min/experiment, 100 experiments, 5 seeds: vanilla 7.1%, propose-many 6.9%, select 8.4%, Rehearse 10.7% mean improvement.
  quote: "selecting rather than taking the first lifts the final improvement to 8.4%. The store adds further improvement, to 10.7% (+2.3pp over select)"
  where: Sec 5.2 p8
  Extra: Rehearse cut val bpb by 8.9% at experiment 30 vs vanilla 3.3%. Much of that early gap comes from one batch-size reduction.
- Generalization. CIFAR-10 (glm-5.1) accuracy gain 2.85% vs vanilla 2.10%. ETTh1 (deepseek-v4) MSE cut 54.0% vs 40.1%. Rehearse reaches vanilla's final level after 54 (CIFAR) and 63 (ETTh1) experiments, versus 100. Rehearse ends ahead on 9 of 10 seeds. ETTh1 spread ±3.0 vs ±11.2.
  quote: "Rehearse ends ahead on 9 of 10 additional-loop runs."
  where: Sec 5.3 p8, Table 4 p16
- Late-run returns diminish in AutoSOTA logs: helpful modifications fall from 70% (iterations 1-2) to 43% (iteration 6+); mean gain shrinks from 3.6% to 0.3%.
  where: Abstract, Fig 4 (App H p17)
- Pre-run judgment is useful without memory: 79.5% selective accuracy on 296 same-baseline pairs. With the store: 84.2%. Both-worked ranking pairs: 67.4% to 74.1%.
  quote: "selective accuracy rises from 79.5% without the store to 84.2% with it"
  where: Sec 4.3, 4.5 p6-8
- Memory is candidate-level, not a direction blacklist. Weight decay lowered 0.2 to 0.15 was reverted; raising it was kept across 4 values. 87% of Rehearse's kept changes came from families that also had did-not-work attempts. A no-LLM "farther from failed attempts" rule scores 47.8% on the deep bucket (n=23).
  where: Sec 5.4 p9, App F p16
- Strict consensus (judge both orders, abstain on disagreement) cuts run-to-run spread from 5.1 to 1.7 points.
  where: Sec 4.2 p6
- Calibration: with a worked rate of 20%, N=5, K=1, expected success@1 is 61.2% (Rehearse) vs 54.3% (no memory) vs 20.0% (random). Model-based, not measured.
  where: Table 5, App I p18

MECHANISM (for the note)
Propose-Predict-Execute. Propose N=5 candidates, each with description, hypothesis, implementation, type. Run a pairwise tournament in both orders (2*C(5,2)=20 judge calls per step). Run top k=1. Record change plus binary outcome. Retrieval: same task, earlier attempts only, cosine >= 0.40 with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dim); one line per precedent, change plus worked/did-not-work. Store is plain files. No fine-tuning and no change to the training code. Worked = strictly improves the accepted baseline. Crashes and timeouts count as did-not-work.

LIMITS (authors)
- Depth variable n_baseline is observational, not randomized causal. Headroom, modification family and difficulty vary with depth.
- Only 3 loops with measurable outcomes, 5 seeds each. Model and task are paired (one model per loop), so effects are not separated.
- Budget counts training runs only. Proposal and judge inference are excluded (20 judge calls per step).
- Rehearse only selects from proposer candidates. Other memory forms and candidate counts are untested live. Longer runs and other pool sizes are untested.
- Benchmark corpus comes from one LLM optimizer (AutoSOTA). Model names are serving aliases, not frozen checkpoints.
- Memory baselines are adaptations, not reproductions. Authors are from Tencent, using Tencent models. Code and benchmark are "will release", not yet available.
- Cliff-bucket sample is small (cliff n is not stated; the heuristic baseline used n=23 decided).

BUILDS ON: Karpathy 2026 autoresearch/nanochat loop; AutoSOTA (Li et al. 2026, Tsinghua FIB Lab); ForeAgent (Zheng et al. 2026, pairwise pre-execution filtering); AIDE (Jiang et al. 2025); Reflexion (Shinn et al. 2023); Self-Refine (Madaan et al. 2023); Generative Agents (Park et al. 2023); MemGPT (Packer et al. 2023); Voyager (Wang et al. 2024a); selective prediction (Geifman & El-Yaniv 2017); position bias in LLM judges (Zheng et al. 2023); FunSearch, AlphaEvolve; Landesberg 2026 (judge agreement does not predict best-of-N).

CODE: Algorithm 1 (App A p14): while budget: C<-PROPOSE(s_t); c*<-PREDICT(C,s_t,M); run c*; M<-M U {RECORD(c*,r)}; if r improves, commit patch, else discard.
Judge output: {"winner": "A"|"B", "confidence": 0.5--1.0, "reasoning": "..."} (App C p15).

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p2): selective accuracy vs n_baseline with coverage on the right axis. Best single picture of the cliff.
- Fig 2 (p5): Propose-Predict-Execute overview.
- Fig 3 (p9): best-so-far improvement curves in 3 live loops.
- Fig 4 (p17): diminishing returns in AutoSOTA logs. Table 1 (p7) and Table 2 (p9) hold the memory comparison.

PLACEMENT: 08-self-improving-loops is over length. Best alternative is 09-failure-modes-and-guardrails: the confidence cliff is a failure mode (judge commits more as it gets less reliable), and the guardrail is focused memory plus strict consensus. Second choice is 03-the-scorekeeper, because the paper is about a pre-run predictor that gates the scorer's expensive run. Do not use 05 or 02. Only a one-line pointer belongs in 08 if the note must mention it. Existing notes have no mention of Rehearse or the confidence cliff (grep found none).

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions. Some words are joined in the extraction (title, "theconfidence cliff"). Figure content was not viewed. The ledger/target dates look consistent: paper is dated 30 Jul 2026, so it is recent.
